moat_against: Tenant concentration — Caesars + MGM roughly 70%+ of rent; Las Vegas roughly half
Single master-lease restructuring would hit cash flow directly
No operating/pricing control — rent growth capped by escalators
Growth externally funded — equity issuance dilutes per-share growth (shares +6.5%/yr)
Rate-sensitive — long-duration rent stream trades like a bond when real yields rise
moat_for: Irreplaceable Strip assets — scarce frontage, extreme replacement cost, gaming-license barriers
~39-40yr weighted-average triple-net lease term with 1-2% fixed or CPI-linked escalators
Triple-net structure — tenants bear taxes, insurance, maintenance
100% occupancy; rent collected in full through COVID
Tenants largely publicly traded operators (77% of rent)
moat_justification: Strong (7/10): irreplaceable Las Vegas Strip assets with extreme replacement cost and gaming-license barriers, locked in by ~39-40-year triple-net leases with 1-2% fixed or CPI-linked escalators, 100% occupancy, and rent collected in full through COVID. Capped below wide-moat because Caesars and MGM together supply roughly 70%+ of rent (Las Vegas roughly half), VICI has no operating or pricing control beyond the escalators, and growth must be bought with external debt and equity, diluting per-share growth.
name: VICI Properties Inc.
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) triple-net landlord with irreplaceable Strip assets and ~40-year leases, but at $23.10 it returns 14.7% weighted — just under the 15% hurdle; it clears 15% at or below its weighted IV@15% of $22.58, with tenant concentration and 6.3x net debt/OE as the standing risks.
sector: Real Estate — experiential / gaming triple-net REIT
